YouTube title seed: How Does a Key Actually Open a Lock?
YouTube description seed: Your key has a pattern of cuts. Guess what each one is pushing on inside the lock. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: The key's cuts lift tiny split pins until every split lines up, and only then can the lock turn.
The later surprise: A wrong key leaves pins crossing the line, so even a key that looks almost right stays stuck.
The very first frame shows two near-identical brass keys lying still side by side next to a front-door lock, viewed from the side; only the camera moves, a slow push-in. The camera is already moving in the first frame, and nothing in the first second gives the answer away.

Scene 1 (contradiction, 0-6s): Opening: side view, the brass key slides into the front-door lock. Camera: slow push-in. Only these objects in frame: brass key, front-door lock, door. No food, no faces, no extra items.
Scene 2 (clue, 6-12s): No answer yet; this scene only deepens the mystery. A real clear acrylic practice lock (real parts only, no animation or cutaway graphics) held still in soft daylight, the uneven row of pins visible, the key lying beside it with its cuts in profile. Scene 3 (mechanism, 12-18s): The key slides into the clear practice lock and the pin pairs rise until the splits line up. Camera: static close-up, slight push-in. Only these objects in frame: clear acrylic practice lock, pins, key. No food, no faces, no extra items.
Scene 4 (second_reveal, 18-24s): A hand tries to turn a nearly identical wrong key in the clear practice lock; the plug stays stuck with pins at uneven heights. Camera: slow push-in. Only these objects in frame: clear acrylic practice lock, pins, wrong key, hand. No food, no faces, no extra items.

facts.statement: In a pin tumbler lock, pairs of small spring-loaded pins sit across the line between the turning plug and the fixed housing, and that blocks the plug from turning.
The cuts on the right key lift each pin pair just enough that the split between the two pins lines up with that line, so the plug can turn and move the bolt.
A wrong key lifts the pins to the wrong heights, so some pins still cross the line and the plug stays stuck.
